title: CDC says honey before the first birthday can cause infant botulism
summary: CDC says not to give honey to a child younger than 12 months, including on a pacifier or in formula.
body: The CDC page on foods and drinks to avoid or limit, dated 14 April 2026, says honey given to children younger than 12 months may cause a severe food poisoning called botulism. It says not to give honey before 12 months, and not to add honey to the baby's food, water, infant formula, or pacifier. This is a warning about a bacterial illness in infants, not a note that honey is unclean in general. The page is United States guidance. It does not describe how to treat botulism. A child who is ill needs a clinician, not this card.
